caption: Acts explicitly applies Psalm 2’s conspiring rulers to Herod, Pilate and Jesus’s opponents. It is a strong Christian reuse of an older royal psalm.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did rulers conspire against Jesus? Psalm 2 pictures kings joining together against God and His anointed ruler. Acts applies those words to Jesus’s opponents.
slides.body: Psalm 2 pictures kings joining together against God and His anointed ruler. Acts applies those words to Jesus’s opponents.
slides.heading: Did rulers conspire against Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 2:1-3: The rulers gather together, against the LORD and against His Anointed One.
slides.body: The rulers gather together, against the LORD and against His Anointed One.
slides.heading: Ps 2:1-3

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Acts 4:25–28, BSB: Herod and Pontius Pilate … conspired against Your holy Servant Jesus, whom You anointed.
slides.body: Herod and Pontius Pilate … conspired against Your holy Servant Jesus, whom You anointed.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Acts 4:25–28

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Acts makes the link explicit It names Herod and Pilate as the rulers who gathered against Jesus. This is a clear New Testament application.
slides.body: It names Herod and Pilate as the rulers who gathered against Jesus. This is a clear New Testament application.
slides.heading: Acts makes the link explicit

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The psalm began with an older king Its first setting is rebellion against God’s installed ruler. Acts treats Jesus as the pattern’s fullest example.
